the performance of nondata- aided symbol timing delay estimat ors for linearly modu lated waveforms transmitted through a flat-fading channel improves as the pulse-shape bandwidth increases, while the performance of non data-aided carrier frequenc y offset estimators is independent of the oversampling factor and pulse-shape bandwidth.

the performance of the nondata-aid (NDA) estimator is independent of the oversampling factor and is a function of the bandwidth of the pulse shape.
the accuracy of the estimators is inversely proportional to the oversampling factor and proportional to the pulse shape bandwidth.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the performance of the proposed estimators is not affected by the oversampling factor, and the performance of the symbol timing estimators improves as a function of pulse shape bandwidth
the estimators are asymptotically efficient and their performance is not affected by the oversampling factor
the performance of the estimator for symbol timing delay is independent of the frequency offset and the performance of the frequency offset estimator is independent of the symbol timing delay.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, for a given oversampling factor and pulse shape, the symbol timing delay and carrier frequency offset estimators perform equally well, and their performance is independent of the oversampling factor.
the accuracy of symbol delay estimators improves with increasing bandwidth of the pulse shape, while the accuracy of the frequency offset estimators does not.

these estimators are capable of providing accurate estimates of the carrier frequency offset and the symbol timing delay for a large class of linearly modulated signals transmitted through a flat-fading channel.
